result.title: April 2018
result.summary: Contra Costa County Employees’ Retirement Association (CCCERA) issued an April 2018 request for proposals for master custodian and related services. The RFP was issued April 13; proposer questions were due April 24, with responses and addenda expected online by May 8; proposals were due May 25. Proposal evaluations, finalist interviews and/or site visits were planned from late May through late July, with a Board recommendation anticipated August 22. Questions and clarification requests had to be emailed by 5 p.m. Pacific Time on April 24 to RFP@cccera.org, identifying the custodian bank and questioner, plus the relevant RFP section and page. The RFP and compiled questions, responses, and addenda were available at cccera.org; an electronic copy could be requested by email. Proposals must follow the RFP’s submission instructions. CCCERA’s address and phone and fax numbers are provided.

result.title: Master Custodian RFP Schedule and Questions
result.summary: The page lists the RFP schedule: issuance April 13, 2018; proposer questions due April 24; responses expected May 8; proposals due May 25; evaluations, finalist interviews and/or site visits from late May through late July; and anticipated Board approval recommendation August 22. Questions or clarification requests must be emailed to RFP@cccera.org by 5 p.m. Pacific Time April 24. Each must identify the custodian bank and submitter, plus the relevant RFP section and page. Email is preferred. CCCERA will post compiled questions and responses, along with any addenda, on www.cccera.org by 5 p.m. Pacific Time May 8.

OBTAINING COPIES OF RFP

2REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS FOR MASTER CUSTODIAN AND RELATED SERVICES

result.title: TABLE OF CONTENTS
result.summary: The table of contents lists the RFP’s introduction, background, services, minimum qualifications, proposal completion and submission procedures, submissions, evaluation, Questionnaire (Attachment A), fee schedule (Attachment B), and draft contract, with page references. CCCERA seeks one qualified vendor to provide comprehensive domestic and international master custody and related investment services, including safekeeping, settlement, valuation, performance measurement, foreign exchange, income collection, securities lending, and management, accounting, and information systems. Partial bids and subcontracted services are not accepted, though CCCERA may make a split award or select no proposer. The contract will be completed after final selection. Proposals must follow the RFP’s section and question order; misleading or false information may lead to disqualification or termination of a resulting contract.

result.title: II. BACKGROUND
result.summary: CCCERA, established by Contra Costa County in 1945, provides retirement, disability, death, and survivor benefits for county employees and 16 participating agencies under CERL and PEPRA. It is governed by state law, Board policies, and permitted County Board of Supervisors resolutions. Its 12-member Board manages the system: five members are appointed, four elected by active members, two elected by retirees, and the county treasurer serves ex officio; three seats are alternates. Members other than the treasurer serve three-year terms without term limits. The Board controls investments and sets objectives, strategies, and policies. Its Investment Policy Statement governs an $8.5 billion traditional and alternative portfolio, including asset allocation aligned with expected liabilities. CCCERA’s Functionally Focused Portfolio dedicates funds for 48 months of projected benefits, with remaining assets in growth and diversifying allocations. In 2017, the liquidity portfolio was fully funded through three short-duration fixed-income managers producing monthly benefit-payment cash flows, while growth and diversifying portfolios were repositioned. Related information is available on CCCERA’s website.

result.title: III. SERVICES TO BE PROVIDED
result.summary:
III. SERVICES TO BE PROVIDED
For master custodial services, the Proposer is expected to be able to provide all of the services listed below unless otherwise indicated. CCCERA reserves the right to award less than all of the services to the winning Proposer, in its discretion and subject to the agreement of the awardee(s):

result.title: A. Accounting
result.summary: Accounting requirements include trade-date, local- and U.S.-dollar accounting for all securities and full accrual accounting for all assets. Services must cover dividends, interest, corporate actions, securities lending, domestic and international fixed-income and equity portfolios, dividend reinvestment, options, futures and multicurrency derivatives, private placements, alternative and limited-partnership investments, commingled and hedge funds, and real estate and REIT portfolios. Post dividends, bond interest and principal, and mortgage pass-through interest and paydowns on payable dates. Use a January–December fiscal year, maintain a secondary security-pricing source, and report investments at cost and market value, recognizing gains and losses on sales using average cost. Notify CCCERA of corporate actions requiring decisions. Reconcile custodian and investment-manager records daily or monthly, and report material variances with reconciliation steps, adjustments, or justification for unresolved differences.

result.title: B. Securities Settlement
result.summary:
B. Securities Settlement
1. Participating member and access to securities settlement through Depository Trust Company, Federal Reserve wire system, and at other depositories (both domestic and international).
2. The ability to settle physically held securities.
3. The ability to execute foreign exchange transactions.
4. Electronic access to trade and holding data by any CCCERA approved vendors.
5. Settlement on a delivery versus payment basis.

result.title: C. Cash Management
result.summary:
C. Cash Management
1. Provide a Short Term Investment Fund (STIF) for daily cash sweeps. Maintain daily sweep activity for the purpose of transferring uncommitted funds from the individual external manager custody accounts.
2. Income earned by STIF or other cash accounts must be compounded daily.
3. Income earned, redemptions and maturities must be credited to the proper account.
4. Cash flow from purchases and sales must be credited on contractual settlement date.
5. At the direction of CCCERA, provide overnight investment management services for the funds received too late to be invested.
6. Provide same day settlement of cash trades.
7. Transfer cash between accounts, and make and accept wire transfers of funds and ACH transfers of funds.
8. Provide a Cash Flow Model allowing the custodian to process all capital calls and distributions electronically including electronic fund transfers between client accounts.
7

result.title: D. Securities Lending
result.summary: The securities lending program covers eligible domestic and international securities; approved borrower lists, borrowing limits, and ongoing qualification reviews; and collateral requirements using mutually acceptable cash, securities, or letters of credit. U.S. loans require collateral of at least 102% and non-U.S. loans 105% of market value, including accrued income, while maintaining competitive market collateralization. Collateral is monitored daily and topped up when below acceptable mark-to-market levels. All interest and other distributions on loaned securities are collected. Daily reports identify required and pledged collateral, and monthly reports detail lending activity, outstanding loans, and amounts by borrower. CCCERA may decline to lend to any proposed borrower and receives indemnification against borrower default.

result.title: E. Directed Brokerage Services
result.summary:
E. Directed Brokerage Services
1. Provide directed brokerage services for specific CCCERA investment managers.
2. Establish contractual relationships with various domestic and international brokerage firms.
3. Notify CCCERA investment managers of the brokerage firms available for directed brokerage (commission recapture) services.
84. Coordinate and monitor directed brokerage activities on behalf of
CCCERA.
5. Collect rebated brokerage fees and make distribution quarterly.
6. Provide monthly report on individual investment manager activities.

result.title: F. Corporate Actions, Class Actions and Proxy Processing
result.summary:
F. Corporate Actions, Class Actions and Proxy Processing
1. Provide company annual reports, proxy voting cards and proxy statements to CCCERA or designated investment managers prior to annual and special meetings for U.S. and foreign corporations.
2. Provide proxy-voting capabilities for U.S. and foreign holdings, including proxy-voting services, notification of proxy information and translation of foreign proxies.
3. Provide reports detailing all proxy voting activities.
4. Provide notification of pending corporate actions, including conversion privileges, issuance of rights, mergers, tender offers, reorganizations, other actions requiring decisions and applicable legislative actions.
5. Provide notifications of class action litigation and provision of the necessary securities information.
6. File claims for securities class action awards and monitor collection of the amounts to which the Plan is entitled.

result.title: G. Technology
key_items: F. Corporate Actions, Class Actions and Proxy Processing
result.summary: Provide a web-enabled system integrating access management and accounting data to report current and historical performance, prices, market values and international-security exchange rates; composite portfolios; agreed transactions and holdings by security, account, asset class or aggregate; performance aggregates and analytics; pending class-action exposures, filings and deadlines; customized reports and ad hoc queries. The system must monitor compliance with California law and Board investment limits and support disaster recovery and business continuity.

result.title: H. Report Requirements
result.summary: The provider must deliver monthly balance sheets, income statements, performance reports with current and historical market and portfolio data, and reconciliations to Investment Consultant accounting reports, with copies due within 10 days after month-end. Annual holdings, transactions, and investment-data reports are due within 30 calendar days after December 31. Reports must be available electronically and include largest stock and bond holdings, broker commissions by manager/group, service class, broker, cost dollar, and share, and access to daily domestic trade statuses. December 31 reports must meet applicable GASB requirements, including Statements 40, 53, 67, and 72. The provider must annually supply audited internal-control reports for IT and fund accounting systems, plus requested bridge letters; provide other reports CCCERA requests; and notify CCCERA of material variances in manager reconciliations with supporting explanations.

result.title: I. Personnel
result.summary:
I. Personnel
1. Proposer shall assign appropriate accounting and investment performance personnel to the CCCERA account and make assigned personnel available as needed. Additionally, assigned personnel should be available to meet with CCCERA staff at dates and times determined by CCCERA at least semi-annually, or more frequently if required by CCCERA, to discuss services related to CCCERA’s needs.
2. Proposer must make presentations to the Board as required to discuss services related to CCCERA.
3. Proposer shall provide competent personnel to facilitate access to records and information that may be required for audit purposes.
4. Proposer shall provide the personnel to assist CCCERA’s auditor with any and all investment inquiries.
11

result.title: IV. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
result.summary: Proposers must be legally authorized to provide the required custody and asset-management services in California; have at least 30 defined-benefit custodial clients, including 10 public funds with at least $1 billion each in tax-exempt assets; and have 10 years’ custody experience. The proposed account administrator needs five years’ custody experience, including three with the proposer. Proposers must issue annual SOC reports, complete the questionnaire, maintain specified liability, workers’ compensation, banker’s professional liability, and directors’ and officers’ insurance, and provide their own facilities, equipment, supplies, and staff. Complete proposals were due by 5 p.m. PT May 25, 2018; late or misdirected submissions may be rejected. Exceptions must accompany proposals and may be rejected, especially if substantial; the final contract incorporates the RFP, draft contract, and winning proposal. A committee reviews and ranks proposals; finalists may present or host site visits, and the Board selects. CCCERA may amend the RFP, request information or proposals, accept or reject proposals, renegotiate fees, and award all, part, none, or split the contract.

result.title: Proposal Submission and Evaluation Procedures
key_items: V. PROPOSAL COMPLETION AND SUBMISSION PROCEDURES
result.summary: Vendors must submit fully completed proposals. The final contract will incorporate the RFP, attached draft contract, and winning proposal without substantial deviation. Any requested deviations must be submitted as Exceptions with the proposal; CCCERA may grant or reject them. Substantial exceptions may make a proposal non-responsive and subject to rejection, though CCCERA may allow their withdrawal to cure the issue. Proposals are due by 5:00 p.m. PT on Friday, May 25, 2018; late or incorrectly delivered proposals may be rejected at CCCERA’s discretion. An evaluation committee will examine, rank, and recommend proposals that best meet the RFP’s purposes. Finalists may be asked to present orally, and the committee may request site visits. The Board makes the final evaluation and selection.

result.title: C. Rights Reserved
key_items: V. PROPOSAL COMPLETION AND SUBMISSION PROCEDURES; A. Deadline for Proposals
V. PROPOSAL COMPLETION AND SUBMISSION PROCEDURES
result.summary: CCCERA may amend the RFP before selecting a successful proposer and allow all proposers to revise their proposals. It may request additional information and accept or reject proposals without giving reasons. The Board may request more proposals, renegotiate lower fees at any time, and award all, part, none, or split the contract. CCCERA may inspect facilities before award and reject proposers whose submitted evidence or investigation shows they are unqualified. To encourage participation, CCCERA may notify potential vendors; that outreach gives recipients no scoring preference and does not disadvantage vendors who are not contacted.

result.title: D. Notice to Proposers Regarding Responsibility for Costs
result.summary:
D. Notice to Proposers Regarding Responsibility for Costs
All costs of preparation and presentation associated with responding to this RFP will be the responsibility of the Proposer. Proposers may be asked to make a presentation before the Board if selected as a finalist or may be asked to host an on-site visit for the evaluation committee. None of the costs associated with submittal of the response to the RFP or associated with the presentation or hosting an on-site visit will be reimbursed by CCCERA.

result.title: E. Notice to Proposers Regarding the Public Records Act
key_items: D. Notice to Proposers Regarding Responsibility for Costs
D. Notice to Proposers Regarding Responsibility for Costs
result.summary: Proposals become CCCERA’s property and are generally subject to California Public Records Act disclosure, though confidential until selection is complete and a contract is awarded. CCCERA may use proposal ideas; withdrawal requires written notice. Proposers must assert any confidentiality claims themselves, and absent a court ruling exempting records, they may be inspected. A proposal is a binding offer governed by California law. Submission accepts the RFP terms, subject to timely exceptions CCCERA may choose to grant. Proposers must disclose finder’s fees or commissions paid or payable to nonemployees. They must acknowledge fiduciary duties under Section 31595 of the 1937 Act when exercising discretion or giving investment advice; accept California law and incorporation of the RFP, response, and follow-up questions into any agreement; serve as CCCERA’s accounting book of record with diligent, timely reporting, third-party data reasonableness checks, and prompt notice of concerns or material variances; and have substantial experience in custodial, securities-lending, and ancillary services.

result.title: G. Acceptance of Terms and Conditions; H. Disclosure of Placement Agent
key_items: G. Acceptance of Terms and Conditions
result.summary:
F. Binding Offer
The Proposer shall be bound by the information and representations contained in any proposal submitted. Said proposal is deemed to be a binding offer on the part of the Proposer. Proposer understands and agrees that California law will govern.
G. Acceptance of Terms and Conditions
Submission of a proposal in response to this RFP evidences the Proposer’s acceptance of the terms and conditions contained within this RFP, subject to any exceptions that the Proposer may properly and timely submit and which CCCERA, in its sole discretion, may grant consistent with the terms of the RFP.
H. Disclosure of Placement Agent
CCCERA requires the disclosure of any payment of a finder’s fee in any form. The Proposer must disclose any finder’s fee or finder’s commission t h a t has been paid or shall be paid to any individual, other than an employee of the Proposer’s organization, from the establishment of this investment relationship with CCCERA.

result.title: I. Proposer’s Acknowledgement and Agreement
key_items: F. Binding Offer; G. Acceptance of Terms and Conditions
G. Acceptance of Terms and Conditions
result.summary: Proposers must acknowledge fiduciary duties and prudence under Section 31595, accept California law, incorporate the RFP and related questions into any services agreement, serve as CCCERA’s accounting book of record with diligent reporting and third-party data reasonableness checks, promptly report concerns or material variances, demonstrate substantial custodial, securities-lending, and ancillary-services experience, and answer all RFP questions. Finalists must demonstrate security and disaster-recovery capabilities, provide personnel and documentation for technical review, and submit a business-continuity plan with updates within three business days. California law governs; litigation must be brought in the specified federal Northern District or Contra Costa Superior Court, and all applicable laws must be followed. Proposers must acknowledge fiduciary duties for asset safekeeping and related services and include their standard custodial fiduciary language. By submitting, they certify no collusion, fraud, kickbacks, inducements, improper benefits to public employees, or unauthorized interactions with procurement officials.

result.title: RFP Response, Security, Legal, and Fiduciary Requirements
key_items: L. Standard of Care / Fiduciary Standard
result.summary: Proposers must answer all RFP questions. Finalists must demonstrate adequate security and disaster-recovery capabilities, provide personnel and documentation to discuss security measures, access software, backup and recovery procedures, and business resumption plans, and submit a business-continuation plan with updates within three business days. California law governs the solicitation and contract; litigation must be brought in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California or Contra Costa County Superior Court. Proposers must comply with applicable federal, state, and local laws. CCCERA expects the proposer to acknowledge fiduciary duties concerning asset safekeeping and related responsibilities, and requests the custodian’s standard language for similar engagements.

result.title: M. Ethics in Public Contracting
key_items: J. Security Procedures/Disaster Recovery; K. Applicable Laws and Courts
L. Standard of Care / Fiduciary Standard
result.summary: Proposers certify their bids are free of collusion, fraud, kickbacks, improper inducements, payments, or unauthorized contact with procurement officials. CCCERA may investigate proposer qualifications and request supporting information. Proposers must disclose recent or anticipated corporate changes. Contracts cannot be assigned without CCCERA’s written consent; the anticipated term is at least five years, but the Board may terminate on 90 days’ notice, with or without cause. All proposers will receive written notice of the final decision; this may be the only communication, and post-deadline inquiries are discouraged. Work product and data produced or compiled under the contract are presumed to belong solely to CCCERA, which must have reasonable access to them.

result.title: Proposer Qualifications and Contract Terms
result.summary: CCCERA may investigate a proposer’s ability to perform and request supporting information. Proposers must disclose recent or anticipated corporate changes, including mergers, acquisitions, financing, or stock issuance. Contracts cannot be assigned without CCCERA’s written consent. The engagement is expected to last at least five years, but the Board may terminate it with 90 days’ notice, with or without cause. All proposers will receive written notice of the Board’s final selection, which may be the Plan’s only communication; inquiries after the proposal deadline are discouraged.

result.title: R. Ownership of Data and Work Product
key_items: N. Qualifications of Proposers; O. Business Continuity; P. Assignment of Contract
result.summary:
R. Ownership of Data and Work Product
There is a presumption that all work product generated for CCCERA under this contract, as well as all data compiled by the Proposer while performing this contract, shall become the sole property of CCCERA. CCCERA must be given reasonable access to all such work product or data compiled by the Proposer in the performance of this contract.

result.title: VI. PROPOSAL SUBMISSIONS
result.summary:
VI. PROPOSAL SUBMISSIONS
A. Proposal Acceptance
Proposals shall be enclosed in a sealed package or box, plainly marked in the upper left hand corner with the name, address, and telephone number of the Proposer submitting the proposal and bear the words "CCCERA RFP-MASTER CUSTODIAL SERVICES." The deadline for receipt of the proposal is 5:00 p.m. PT on Friday, May 25, 2018. Any proposal delivered after the deadline will not be considered. The Proposer shall submit one (1) original proposal, four (4) hard copies of the proposal, and one (1) copy in electronic form.
Proposals are to be emailed to RFP@cccera.org and submitted to:

result.title: Contra Costa County Employees’ Retirement Association
result.summary: Proposals must be mailed or hand-delivered to CCCERA at the stated Concord address; proposers using mail or express delivery are responsible for ensuring arrival by the deadline. Timely proposals become CCCERA property. A proposal may be withdrawn before the deadline by written request, but otherwise remains a firm offer for one year after the acceptance deadline. Proposals should include the specified preceding and following information to demonstrate capabilities. Written clarification questions may be sent to RFP@cccera.org by 5:00 p.m. PT April 24, 2018; answers were expected on CCCERA’s website by May 8, 2018. Respondents must not contact CCCERA staff about the RFP. Submission requires agreement to a CCCERA-discretionary audit of relevant provider books, records, documents, accounting procedures, practices, and other materials.

result.title: B. Proposal Preparation
result.summary: Proposals must follow the format and sequence specified in the RFP, and no corrections or resubmissions are accepted after the deadline except clarifications or additional information requested by CCCERA. Proposers must rely on the RFP and related documents; CCCERA is not responsible for prior employee statements or understandings unless documented there. Proposers should promptly report ambiguities, conflicts, discrepancies, omissions, or other errors in writing to the designated CCCERA email and request clarification or modification. Material changes will be issued to all participating respondents through addenda.

result.title: C. Proposal Content and Sequence
result.summary: Proposal content must follow the specified sequence. The cover letter, on official letterhead and signed by an authorized representative (unsigned proposals may be rejected), must identify the signer’s title and all submitted materials; confirm completeness and minimum qualifications; provide proposer contact details, a one-year irrevocable offer, proposed services and ability to perform, account administrator/primary contact, and federal tax ID. It must disclose relevant regulatory or professional proceedings and litigation from the past three years; certify nondiscrimination, genuine non-collusive pricing and no improper remuneration, and absence of conflicts; disclose current or past-five-year relationships with CCCERA Board members or staff; and identify confidential sections. CCCERA is a public agency; lawful, legitimate confidentiality claims may be honored, but blanket claims will not. Include a numerically ordered table of contents; an executive summary of no more than six pages; and completed Attachment A questionnaire responses, subject to verification, with material false or misleading information grounds for rejection. Keep responses clear and brief, follow RFP order, and reproduce each question before answering. Submit fees in U.S. dollars using Attachment B formats; material deviations may cause rejection.

result.title: Proposal Declarations and Submission Requirements
result.summary: Proposers must certify that their proposal is free from fraud or collusion and that they have neither offered nor received related finder’s fees or inducements; disclose any actual or potential conflicts of interest and personal or business relationships, including prospective business negotiations, with CCCERA Board members or staff during the past five years. Proposals must include a numerically ordered table of contents and a concise executive summary of no more than six pages. Proposers must complete the relevant Attachment A questionnaire; responses may be verified, and material false or misleading information may result in rejection. Proposals should be complete, clear, brief, follow the RFP’s order, and reproduce each question in full before answering.

result.title: 5. Fee Schedule
result.summary: Fees must be submitted in U.S. dollars using Attachment B’s required formats; material deviations may lead to rejection. Fees must cover all RFP services, remain guaranteed for five years, may be refined after selection, and cannot exceed the proposal amount. Proposers must identify and explain any exceptions or state that none exist. They must list clients receiving similar custodial services and provide contact details for at least three references, plus details of pension clients whose contracts ended in the past five years, including name, size, termination date, and reason. Optional promotional material may be included separately, but not information responding directly to service requirements. CCCERA prohibits contact with Board members about the RFP during selection except at relevant public meetings; staff contact is limited to prescribed or CCCERA-initiated communications. An evaluation committee will review proposals. Questions and clarification requests go to RFP@cccera.org, and CCCERA will share responses and inquiries with relevant proposers.

result.title: Fees, Exceptions, Experience, and References
result.summary: Proposed fees must cover all RFP services, remain guaranteed for five years, and cannot be increased after selection, though they may be refined based on relevant factors. Proposers must identify and explain any exceptions or deviations, or state that none exist. They must list clients receiving similar custodial services and provide contact details for at least three references. They must also disclose pension plan clients whose custodial contracts ended in the past five years, including each client’s name, size, termination date, and reason.

result.title: 8. Other Information
result.summary: Section 8 is optional for supplementary information, such as promotional brochures, but must not contain material directly responding to service requirements. CCCERA states it provided enough information to prepare proposals. While selection is pending, proposers may not contact Board members except at a public meeting where the selection is on the agenda; contact with procurement staff is limited to the methods specified or staff-initiated contact. An evaluation committee will assess proposals. Questions or clarification requests must be emailed to RFP@cccera.org, and CCCERA will share its responses and the original inquiries with all relevant proposers or potential proposers.

result.title: VII. PROPOSAL EVALUATION PROCESS
key_items: D. Business Stability; E. Assigned Individuals; F. Fee Proposal; G. General quality and adequacy of Proposal,
G. General quality and adequacy of Proposal,
result.summary: CCCERA may seek additional information or clarification from reasonably qualified proposers on issues such as fees and personnel availability; proposer-specific issues remain confidential unless disclosure is legally required. After clarification, scores are finalized and a tentative award goes to the proposal most advantageous under the stated criteria. CCCERA may narrow the field and conduct interviews or due-diligence visits. Proposals are first screened against minimum qualifications, with noncompliant proposals eliminated. Evaluation considers service capabilities (risk and cash management, accounting and reconciliation, performance analytics, reporting, securities lending, year-end reporting, GASB support, and transition/conversion); comparable experience and custodial expertise, especially for public entities and 1937 Act, U.S. and non-U.S. services; qualified staff and assigned individuals’ credentials; business stability, reputation, professionalism, and succession planning; fee reasonableness and competitiveness; proposal quality, completeness, compliance, and delivery plan; client references; and any other factors in CCCERA’s best interest.

result.title: VIII. QUESTIONNAIRE – ATTACHMENT A
key_items: A. ORGANIZATION, ADMINISTRATION AND GENERAL INFORMATION
result.summary: Attachment A requests a comprehensive profile of the proposer’s Institutional Master Trust/Custody business: executive overview, competitive strengths, public-fund services, organizational charts and management structure. It seeks client and asset counts by client type and size, definition of “Other,” nontraditional investment percentages, five-year client and asset gains/losses and termination reasons, staffing by function, turnover, relationship-officer workloads and support arrangements, response and follow-up processes, and plans for staffing and client growth. It asks about product-development spending, personnel and plans; service-quality programs and survey results; business-unit revenue and profit shares over five years; financial stability, assets, capital, ratings and annual report; relevant litigation and investigations; and insurance coverage. Further questions address responsibility for unusual client solutions and possible fees, client education and manager funding, regulatory monitoring and communication, fiduciary scope and limits, auxiliary services, and three large U.S. defined-benefit plan references.

result.title: B. PERFORMANCE MEASUREMENT, ANALYTICS AND COMPLIANCE
result.summary: The questionnaire asks for performance-measurement client counts by client type; portfolios represented and approximate assets; group staffing; domestic and international systems, including global results before and after currency adjustments; calculation methodology; daily through annual gross- and net-of-fee reporting, online availability after month-end, custom reports, and custom benchmarks. It covers risk-analytics capabilities, whether included or separately priced, available services and fees; systems for processing, valuing, and reporting alternative assets; and guideline-compliance monitoring, including online availability, client uptake, accuracy and violation notifications, custodian assistance and training, monitorable rules, commingled funds, portfolio characteristics, and customization limits. It also asks about unique services, how they complement or overlap with consultant-provided services, and available comparison indexes and universes, their sources, and how and when they are received.

result.title: C. INVESTMENT MANAGER RELATIONS (Investment Reconciliation Process)
result.summary: The questionnaire asks about investment-manager information systems and how they differ from client systems, real-time account access, trade-instruction channels and deadlines, and competitive advantages in handling manager hires and terminations. It covers whether a dedicated liaison group manages reconciliations, its structure and coordination with accounting, or how relationships are otherwise managed. It asks about reconciliation responsibilities, procedures, timing relative to report mailing, formal process and frequency, pricing and market-value research, proactive coordination, and client communication of exceptions, including the ability to reconcile daily. It also addresses pricing-discrepancy tolerances and resolution; corporate-action cost allocation and rate disputes; commission-recapture reconciliation and brokerage delays; and whether dedicated accounting staff reconcile exceptions with alternative-investment general partners or managers, including differences for non-traditional managers.

result.title: D. ACCOUNTING & REPORTING
result.summary: A questionnaire assessing a custodian’s accounting and reporting systems, including automation; interest and dividend payments; mortgage-security pricing, paydowns and accounting; fee validation and fund identification; and extensive alternative-investment accounting, valuation, transactions, partnership administration, staffing, technology, services and fees. It asks about reports and feeds, delivery timelines, accruals, stale prices, accuracy controls, corrections, data transfer, cost-basis methods, gains and losses, commission recapture, outsourcing, retention and proxy-voting support. It covers GASB reporting and readiness, online access, custom and real-time reporting, help desk, daily valuation and reconciliation, general-ledger feeds, derivatives, failed trades and exchange rates. It also addresses report timeliness and special reporting, foreign-exchange fiduciary duties, execution controls and fees, and class-action monitoring, filings, recoveries, prior-custodian transitions, controls, staffing, interfaces and charges. Finally, it asks about foreign-tax reclaim processing, monitoring, reconciliations and fees.

result.title: E. SECURITY MOVEMENT AND CONTROL
result.summary: The questionnaire asks about depository memberships and services; asset registration and custody; automation and location of security processing and physical settlement; securities lost or misplaced; custody and settlement staffing and reporting; corporate-action processing; purchase-fail float, fail rates, account compensation, cash effects, and manager notifications. It covers income collection, timely settlement, reinvestment availability, proxy transmission, abnormal-price controls and tolerances, and client-selected pricing sources. It also requests pricing sources by asset class, investigation of significant price changes, pricing of unlisted and difficult securities (including private placements and bank loans), update frequency, and use of matrix pricing. Finally, it asks about brokerage capabilities in transition trades and crossing, alternative prime brokerage products, and fund administration services.

result.title: F. SYSTEM CAPABILITIES & DISASTER RECOVERY
result.summary: A questionnaire asks about Master Trust/Custody system capabilities and disaster recovery: existing hardware configuration, age, access restrictions and controls; backup and restore capacity, data-retrieval time, business continuity plans, testing frequency and last test, use in the past three years, longest outage and cause, and preventive measures. It also covers hot-site and personnel backup locations, external review of recovery plans, software development and support arrangements and vendors, significant recent changes to core accounting and security movement/control systems and their implementation dates, planned enhancements and timelines, security procedures, downtime in the past year and normal availability hours, and whether domestic and global accounting use one multicurrency system.

result.title: G. CASH MANAGEMENT
result.summary: The questionnaire asks about cash-management options, including tax-exempt short-term funds, managers, guidelines, objectives, fees, performance histories, and expense ratios; sweep and other fees; daily cash-investment procedures and automation; timing and exceptions for STIF interest, purchase debits, sale credits, and reinvestment of receipts; and whether missed dividends are made good. It also covers wire and book-transfer instructions and deadlines, use of separate cash managers, cash forecasting, reimbursement for erroneous overnight debits, overdraft notifications, charges and investigation practices, investment and interest-bearing currencies and related charges, required balances at sub-custodians, and countries where standard policies do not apply.

result.title: H. CONVERSION
result.summary: The section requests details of the custody conversion process, including an estimated schedule, tasks and timelines for the client and Master Custodian, and any conversion manual. It asks what personnel, equipment, training, consultants, procedures, and controls will support an accurate, timely conversion; expected duration; contingency plans and remedies for delays; and how transition staff coordinate with permanent account administrators. It also asks how in-process transactions, claims, and performance measurement files are handled; whether historical data can be backloaded and at what cost; specific problems and solutions from transitions in the past year; anticipated conversion problems and their resolution; and any fees or costs for moving to or from the provider.

result.title: I. SECURITIES LENDING
result.summary: A comprehensive securities-lending due-diligence questionnaire covering program establishment, direct or third-party provision, philosophy, market share, scale, markets, electronic capabilities, client eligibility and participation, and fair loan allocation and income sharing. It requests asset-class utilization, spreads, earnings, cash-collateral yields, investment vehicles, guidelines, fees, and sample reports and contracts. Topics include accepted collateral; borrower and issuer credit assessment, limits and monitoring; stress testing, defaults, pool losses and NAV breaches; collateral, market, liquidity, settlement and operational risks; indemnification; sale fails; and recall and mark-to-market procedures. It examines third-party support, legal and bankruptcy risks, foreign regulation, coordination with investment managers, lending to custodians, and income crediting. It also addresses systems, communications, online reporting, controls, staff separation, training, audits, performance benchmarking, and anticipated industry changes.

result.title: J. GLOBAL CUSTODY
result.summary: The questionnaire requests details on an organization’s global custody services: ability to custody separately managed non-U.S. assets and related fees; service history, assets, clients, capabilities, and software; responsibilities across headquarters, overseas offices, and sub-custodians; country coverage, agents, assets, selection, review, risk assessment, and terminated relationships. It asks about depositories, clearing, settlement communications and funding, foreign exchange services and reporting, income collection, tax receivables and reclaims, multi-currency accounting for forward contracts and options, reconciliations, controls, insurance, market-practices manuals, and segregated accounts. It also seeks reporting currencies and exchange-rate methods, foreign-exchange revenue, failed-trade handling and settlement statistics, and domestic/international class-action tracking, claims, appointment and termination procedures, eligibility, updates, reconciliation, system differences, and fees. Finally, it requests the safekeeping network’s market coverage, sub-custodian names, and assets held.

result.title: K. AUDIT CONTROLS
result.summary: The questionnaire asks who monitors audit recommendations to management, how the process works, and for a recent example; requests the latest 10-K and 8-K filings and SSAE 16/SAS 70, SOC 1, and available SOC 2 reports; seeks independent auditor internal-control opinions on custody services from the past three years; asks whether CCCERA staff and contracted auditors can access corporate audit reports and internal-audit workpapers; requests credit ratings from all rating agencies for the past four fiscal years, identifying the rated company segment; and asks whether and to what extent external audits cover trust-department records and procedures, what certification accompanies annual reports, and whether client auditors may examine bank records related to client accounts.

result.title: L. Technology
result.summary: The section asks about the company’s technology capabilities and strategy: the systems enhancement team’s size, structure, and service model; the process for evaluating and implementing technology enhancements; and quality-control and testing teams, standards, and a specific example from a technology-driven product launch or enhancement in the past year. It requests details of enhancements implemented over the past year and planned for the next one to three years in core accounting, corporate actions, trade processing, benefit payments, and performance and analytics, including the business processes affected and expected benefits to client experience. It also asks whether any technology units are outsourced and whether joint ventures or outside contractors contribute to the technology strategy, including their roles in enhancement and production processes.

result.title: M. Core Custody and Accounting and Performance/Analytics
result.summary: The questionnaire asks providers to explain their custody, accounting, and performance-analytics business model, team functions and interactions, service differentiators, planned and past organizational changes, client satisfaction trends, team experience, quality control, and staffing changes. It requests five recent products and five planned innovations; service tiers, benefits, costs, reporting timelines, SLAs, incentives, quality and satisfaction measures, client-shared metrics, data-accuracy controls, and processes for correcting valuation or transaction errors. It also covers relationship-manager caseloads and tiers, stale-asset reporting, security-characteristic data and service options, databases and their integration and controls, and any outsourced or joint-venture arrangements, including evaluation, locations, processing workflows, QC, and turnover. For CCCERA, providers must identify portfolio challenges and solutions, common performance indicators, proposed penalties and incentives with client-use counts, public-pension experience, evidence-backed competitive strengths and beneficiaries, their greatest improvement need, and plans for transparency into alternative-asset holdings, including current and future capabilities.

result.title: IX. ATTACHMENT B MASTER CUSTODIAN AND RELATED SERVICES FEE SCHEDULE
result.summary: Proposers must quote mandatory flat fees for Years 1–5. Year 1 may be higher for transition costs; Years 3–5 receive CPI increases calculated from the Year 2 fee. Proposals are compared first on this basis. Optional unbundled pricing may follow the Section III services list and must include annual not-to-exceed ceilings for Year 1 and Years 2–5, without CPI escalation; Year 1’s ceiling may be higher. Fee schedules are requested for both securities-lending scenarios: lending mandated (bundled), with lending revenue not netted against the flat fee, and lending not mandated (unbundled). Each schedule lists custody fees for Years 1–5. Proposers must also state the securities-lending revenue split between CCCERA and the bank where broker-default indemnification is provided, and address any additional indemnification beyond broker default.

result.title: Mandatory flat-fee (with CPI escalator in years 3-5) and optional a la carte pricing:  all Proposers MUST provide a fee quote on a flat-fee basis.  The flat-fee for Year 1 of the engagement may be higher than following years, to account for transition...
key_items: IX. ATTACHMENT B MASTER CUSTODIAN AND RELATED SERVICES FEE SCHEDULE
result.summary: The schedule requires flat-fee quotes for Years 1–5, with Years 3–5 adjusted for CPI based on Year 2; Year 1 may reflect transition costs. Optional unbundled pricing must include annual not-to-exceed ceilings for Years 1–5 without CPI escalation. Proposers provide fees for custody with and without securities lending, disclose lending revenue splits and indemnification, proposed short-term investment vehicles and expense ratios, and overdraft charges. The questionnaire identifies services included in the flat fee and prices for exclusions: custody and accounting; online access, reporting, performance measurement, analytics and tools; settlement and income collection; transition, conversion and re-registration; penalties and expenses; compliance and risk services; proxy voting and class actions; alternative investments; derivatives valuation and processing; public-records ad hoc reports; and any other charges.

result.title: X. DRAFT CONTRACT
result.summary: The RFP includes a draft custodian contract and asks firms to identify requested exceptions or additions. The agreement is between the Contra Costa County Employees’ Retirement Association (CCCERA) and a California-authorized custodian. Its contents cover custody duties and standards of care; asset handling, accounts, settlements, payments, agents, proxies and instructions; disaster recovery, reporting, fees, title, security codes and taxes; investment-manager authority; term, termination and amendment; representations, notices, governing law, insurance, affirmative action, records, audits, confidentiality, indemnification, securities litigation and foreign exchange; and exhibits. The preamble cites CCCERA’s legal and fiduciary framework and authority to appoint a custodian. CCCERA engages the custodian for delivered Fund assets; the custodian is not responsible for assets not delivered and must notify CCCERA in writing if expected assets are not received within three business days of the anticipated receipt date. The excerpt begins the section on the custodian’s standard of care and duties.

result.title: 2.1 Standard of Care
result.summary: The section sets out CCCERA’s custodial agreement with a California-authorized trust company, recognizing the Board’s fiduciary responsibility and authority to appoint a custodian. It requires professional care in safekeeping and accounting for assets received, with written notice within three business days when expected assets do not arrive; the Custodian is not responsible for assets it never receives. The agreement governs bank accounts, investment instructions, cash investment and reporting, income, reversals, interest, securities lending, and securities custody and release. It also covers purchase and sale settlements, payments, agents, notices, proxies, voting, and reliance on Proper Instructions. Other provisions address anti-self-dealing, disaster recovery, records, accounting, reports, audits, reconciliations, fees, title and third-party information limits, taxes, investment-manager authority, indemnity, class actions, foreign exchange, execution and conflicts, and termination, amendments, transfers, assignment, representations, notices, governing law, insurance, employment, severability, confidentiality, and prior agreements.

nodes.title: CUSTODIAN CONTRACT
nodes.summary: The agreement is between CCCERA, a California retirement association administered by its Board of Trustees, and a trust company authorized to operate in California. It recites the Board’s exclusive fiduciary responsibility for CCCERA assets and CCCERA’s authority to appoint a trust company to safeguard and keep records of its assets. CCCERA engages the Custodian to hold assets delivered to it, its agents, or subcustodians before, at, or after execution; the Custodian is not responsible for assets it does not receive and must notify CCCERA in writing within three business days after an expected asset fails to arrive. The Custodian must perform agreed services, including safekeeping, with the care, skill, diligence, and responsibility of a professional custodian acting in a like capacity.

nodes.title: WITNESSETH:
nodes.summary: The agreement establishes CCCERA under CERL, the Board’s fiduciary role, and appointment of the Custodian to safeguard and account for assets delivered to it, subject to notice requirements, fiduciary care, anti-self-dealing rules, and restrictions on securities custody and release. It governs CCCERA bank accounts, investment instructions, cash investment and reporting, income credits, reversals, interest, and securities lending. Contractual purchase and sale settlement services cover provisional credits and debits, reversals, suspension, payments, agents, notices, proxies, voting, and reliance on Proper Instructions. Other provisions address non-assignment; disaster recovery; accounting, reporting, audits, reconciliations, fees, and recordkeeping; limits on responsibility for title and third-party information; tax and investment-manager authority; termination, amendments, and asset transfers; representations, notices, governing law, insurance, employment, severability, confidentiality, and prior agreements. The Custodian’s indemnity, class-action claims processing and litigation monitoring, foreign-exchange services, execution and conflicts, and execution provisions are also covered.

nodes.title: WITNESSETH: (intro)
nodes.summary: The agreement recites CCCERA’s creation under CERL, the Board’s exclusive fiduciary responsibility, and CCCERA’s authority to appoint a qualified trust company or bank as custodian to safeguard and record its assets. CCCERA appoints the Custodian for assets delivered to it or its agents/subcustodians; it is not responsible for assets not delivered and must notify CCCERA in writing within three business days if expected assets are missing. The Custodian must act with professional-custodian care and as a fiduciary for safekeeping; this standard governs all services and survives termination for six years. Self-dealing is prohibited, except transactions authorized by Proper Instructions; known income from self-dealing must be reported within ten days. Securities must be held for the Fund, including through securities systems, and released only on Proper Instructions or specified standing-instruction events: sales, repurchases, tenders, redemptions, transfers, exchanges, street delivery, reorganizations, rights exercises, derivatives, securities loans, or other instructed purposes. Eligible securities must be registered in the Custodian’s or nominees’ names and delivered in street name or other good-delivery form.

nodes.title: 2.6 Bank Accounts. The Custodian, its agents or its subcustodians may open and maintain a bank account or accounts in the name of CCCERA, Custodian, subcustodian, their
nodes.summary: The Custodian, agents, or subcustodians may open and maintain CCCERA-related bank accounts at their discretion, including with the Custodian’s bank. Accounts hold CCCERA cash, are subject to Investment Manager directions, and require written instructions (not email); withdrawals are made in the Custodian’s custodial capacity. Cash must be invested for CCCERA as soon as reasonably possible upon Proper Instructions. If instructions or repatriation letters are missing, the Custodian must promptly notify CCCERA; any cash remaining uninvested must be explained in the monthly report, including the reason and duration. The Custodian credits income and proceeds when received or, for dividends and interest, under its current payable-date schedule. Advance credits may be reversed if payment is unlikely, with interest charged at the applicable rate, except on assets that remained uninvested in cash. CCCERA must receive written notice of nonpayment, interest charges, and the rate; the rate must be the lowest charged to another client for a comparable purpose and period, and increases apply only to later transactions after notice. Income from securities loans outside the Custodian’s lending program is credited when received. The existing securities-lending agreement in Appendix A remains effective unless amended in writing.

nodes.title: 2.8 Contractual Settlement Services (Purchase/Sales).
nodes.summary: The Custodian provides contractual settlement services for purchases and sales in designated instruments and markets: purchase amounts are debited on customary settlement dates and restored if canceled; sale proceeds receive conditional provisional credit when ordinarily available, subject to instructions, deliverable assets, and expected settlement. The Custodian may suspend services immediately with notice; CCCERA may suspend or terminate them with implementation within five business days. Credits or debits may be reversed if settlement, collection, or instructions are deficient; amounts credited over 30 days may become immediately payable, with applicable interest unless funds remained uninvested in cash. The Custodian may pursue remedies if unable to debit. Fund payments require Proper Instructions and agreed security procedures, covering securities purchases, conversions, expenses, collective funds, foreign exchange, derivatives, securities borrowing, and other specified payments. The Custodian may appoint agents while retaining liability and must notify CCCERA. It forwards proxy and security-related notices; proxies follow CCCERA’s voting instructions, and liability for missed rights is limited by possession, timely instructions, and standard of care. The text defines Proper Instructions, permits specified routine actions without express authority, and protects reasonable reliance on apparently genuine instructions and authority certificates.

nodes.title: 2.16 Non-Assignment. This Agreement shall not be assigned by either party without prior written consent of the other party.
nodes.summary: The agreement bars assignment without written consent and requires disaster recovery, secure backups, and timely plan updates. It sets custody accounting, monthly and annual reporting, audits, investment-manager reconciliations, consultant performance data, and annual compliance reports, with limits on verifying third-party asset reports. Fees follow written schedules, quarterly arrears invoicing, and proration. The custodian disclaims responsibility for asset title and may rely on authenticated instructions; tax duties and investment-manager authority are defined. The agreement covers termination, amendments, asset transfer and successor custodians; party representations and warranties; formal notices; California law and courts; insurance; equal-opportunity employment; severability and written waivers; record access and retention; confidentiality and permitted disclosures; and supersession of prior contracts. The custodian indemnifies CCCERA, subject to claim procedures. It must process securities class-action claims and provide litigation-monitoring data. Foreign-exchange services, execution, conflicts, and responsibilities are addressed. The text concludes with execution provisions and signatures.
